clues.text: This is a town in the far north of South Australia. It sits a long way north of Adelaide.
clues.narrowing: rules out everything outside northern South Australia

source.quote: Coober Pedy () is a town in northern South Australia, 846 km (526 mi) north of Adelaide on the Stuart Highway.

clues.text: The days get so scorching hot here that people build homes under the ground. They live below ground to escape the heat.
clues.narrowing: rules out places without extreme daytime heat

source.quote: Coober Pedy is also renowned for its below-ground dwellings, called "dugouts", which are built in this fashion due to the scorching daytime heat.

clues.text: In 1975, local Aboriginal people adopted a new name for the town. The same word is their name for the mulga tree.
clues.narrowing: rules out towns with no 1975 Aboriginal renaming

source.quote: The name "Coober Pedy" is thought to derive from the Kokatha-Barngarla term kupa-piti, which translates to "whitefellas' hole", but in 1975 the local Aboriginal people of the town adopted the name Umoona, which means "long life" and is also their name for the mulga tree.

clues.text: This town is called the opal capital of the world. That is because of the huge amount of precious opals mined here.
clues.narrowing: rules out all but the top opal mining town

source.quote: The town is sometimes referred to as the "opal capital of the world" because of the quantity of precious opals mined there.

clues.text: A blower truck stands raised above the town sign. It shows how much opal mining shaped this place.
clues.narrowing: confirms it with the blower truck town sign

source.quote: A blower truck is raised above the town sign, representing the importance of opal mining to the town's history.
